title: Tim Dooley — Politics & Geopolitics Compendium
kind: reader-facing political statement synthesis and provenance ledger

method.principle: Separate what Tim explicitly says from accepted formulations, policy proposals, programme design, thought experiments, predictions, research leads, moral judgments, satire, mythology and archive inference.

entries.summary: Cannabis advocacy and later explicit opposition to criminalizing or penalizing drug use; preference for harm differentiation, prevention, rehabilitation and nonjudgmental discussion rather than moral panic.
entries.notes: Do not generalize this into an unrestricted all-drug legalisation doctrine; Tim differentiates psychedelics/mind-expanding drugs from heroin, fentanyl, heavy narcotics and sedatives.

entries.summary: Personal imprisonment and property-rights conflicts become part of the political background and later suspicion of coercive systems.
entries.notes: The archive should not infer a complete criminal-justice philosophy from biography alone.

entries.summary: Prefers democracy / hearing the people or the ‘heart of humanity’; explores AI as an arbiter or coordinator for roles, tasks, hiring and management while preserving individual freedom and human direction.
entries.notes: Capitalism versus socialism remained unresolved in this exchange.

entries.summary: North Axis centered on Tim with Europe, Greenland, Denmark and Canada; America described as a young or adolescent power that may need humility and could become a more regional West-sector power if transatlantic relations are recalibrated. The strongest predictive interpretation is relational/topological: Europe/Canada/North may cohere more strongly while America becomes a more separate western pole.
entries.notes: This mixes diagnosis, prediction and symbolic programme language. It is not a treaty map. Canada-EU SAFE and Canada-Denmark-Greenland defence cooperation were already formalizing by 14 February, and Greenland/U.S. tension was already public. Route detailed prediction scoring to knowledge/timeline/north-axis-greenland-prediction-audit-2025-2026.json.

entries.summary: Israel–Palestine framed morally and symbolically through Cain/Abel language; concern that Israeli policy could deepen war with Iran and possibly Turkey while US Middle East influence declines.
entries.notes: Prediction and symbolic framing are not the same thing as a desired war policy or a final-state settlement plan.

entries.summary: Tim explicitly described a model 'where the north axis and the west go together, and the united states seperates off from europe'.
entries.quote: where the north axis and the west go together, and the united states seperates off from europe
entries.notes: Best read as a directional forecast about alliance topology, not as a prediction that NATO formally dissolves. Later 2026 troop-retrenchment and Greenland/Arctic developments moved materially in this direction.

entries.summary: Tim suspected the United States might retract soldiers from Europe.
entries.quote: we suspect america might retract soliders
entries.notes: Trump publicly entertained troop withdrawals from Italy/Spain 27 days later on April 30. Reuters then reported an actual U.S. pullback from Eastern Europe on July 16, 104 days later. This is the sharpest testable military sub-call within the North-Axis prediction cluster.

entries.summary: US global privileges—dollar hegemony, trade centrality and imperial/security advantages—are paired with obligations such as maritime security. If America withdraws from those obligations, it should accept becoming a nation among nations rather than expecting one-way benefits.
entries.quote: When the troops come home, America becomes a nation among nations.
entries.notes: Not simply anti-American: the core argument is reciprocal obligation. This comes after April 30 withdrawal talk and therefore is not pre-event evidence for that event.

entries.summary: Advocates a sovereign/federated European cloud, compute and data architecture: interoperable national systems, permissioned encrypted exchange, different civil/government/security layers, and multi-vendor alternatives to dependence on Palantir-like platforms.
entries.notes: Tim explicitly separated his mythic/public persona from the serious European architecture and said he had no formal authority over nations.

entries.topic: Shadow power / Epstein / intelligence / NGOs / media
entries.summary: Calls for tracing money, boards, intelligence links, surveillance contracting, NGOs, media influence, lobbying, smear systems and institutional self-protection around Epstein and adjacent power networks.
entries.notes: Research agenda, not proof that adjacent institutions form one coordinated conspiracy. The project standard is to graph sourced relationships and preserve uncertainty.

entries.summary: Public transport can be free at point of use when mobility is socially fundamental, while implementation should avoid thoughtlessly destroying viable private providers.
entries.notes: Useful mixed-economy example: public financing does not automatically require a monopoly provider.

entries.summary: Government should be relatively efficient and no larger than justified, while still supporting welfare, healthcare, education, equality, infrastructure, defense, technology, industry and energy security.
entries.notes: The recurring distinction is not simply big versus small government but capable versus wasteful government.

entries.summary: Favors debt repayment, eventual surplus and disciplined use of public money alongside strategic investment.
entries.notes: Later programme-specific debt targets should not be back-projected as timeless doctrine unless directly adopted.

entries.summary: Describes Denmark as essentially a communal project: social cohesion and reciprocal responsibility are strengths, even while Denmark can be too much of a ‘we’ society and not enough of a ‘me’ society.
entries.quote: I believe Denmark essentially is a communal project ... people have a sense of responsibility towards each other.
entries.notes: The tension between individuality and cohesion is part of the position, not a contradiction to erase.

entries.summary: Values broad liberty around drugs, alcohol, guns and speech while coupling liberty to responsibility, accountability, protection of children/families and social coherence.
entries.notes: Exact gun-control and speech-regulation regimes remain unresolved.

entries.summary: Civic and conduct-based rather than ethnic: noncitizens who commit violent crime, espionage, scams/fraud or serious anti-social conduct may be deportable where lawful; citizenship and whether a person has a lawful destination matter.
entries.notes: Rejects collective ethnic blame. No complete asylum/quota doctrine recovered.

entries.summary: Calls himself ‘radically centered’: taking useful elements from left and right rather than treating either camp as a complete moral or economic system.
entries.notes: Later archive labels such as Nordic civic developmentalism are synthesis labels, not necessarily Tim's own chosen name.

entries.summary: Supports efficient spending, sovereignty, freedom, personal responsibility, education, healthcare, welfare, wealth creation, and a mixture of capitalist and communal mechanisms—explicitly not a doctrinaire socialism.
entries.notes: Outcome/function is preferred over ideological purity.

entries.summary: Anti-dehumanization, anti-authoritarian, anti-trafficking, anti-nihilism, anti-bullying, anti-corruption and anti-fascist while rejecting automatic identification with Antifa. Ideologies are judged by whether they produce domination, radicalization and impunity.
entries.notes: Criticism of Zionism or Nazism is framed as criticism of political ideology/radicalization, not ethnicity or religion.

entries.summary: Restates a broad North field approximately ‘Canada to Turkey minus England’: Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Nordics, much of Europe, Ukraine and Turkey; Russia excluded at that stage, England pending, Mesopotamia possibly later, Australia shared.
entries.notes: Symbolic/programmatic geography, not a claim that these countries formally joined an alliance.

entries.summary: North Programme develops fiscal, procurement, industry, energy, supply-chain, capital-market, Arctic and strategic-independence work. Alignment is offered voluntarily and existing nations remain sovereign.
entries.notes: Distinguish practical programme from sacred North / mythic kingship.

entries.summary: Supports more European/northern gas drilling where economically, legally and environmentally viable in order to improve supply stability.
entries.notes: Later also supports wind, green energy and nuclear; the through-line is resilience rather than a single-fuel ideology.

entries.summary: Supports public schools, hospitals/healthcare, unions, public prisons and a social safety net while also accepting markets, private property, entrepreneurship and contribution/work expectations.
entries.notes: Rejects simplistic unconditional ‘free gibs’; prefers targeted benefits with social/productive return.

entries.summary: Accepts a Radical Center synthesis combining capitalism, welfare, education, healthcare, infrastructure, technology, European capability and democratic order with anti-corruption and anti-extremism.
entries.notes: ‘Civic developmentalism’ is an archive synthesis label.

entries.summary: Wants a stronger northern/European pole with more distance from US dependence: greater European defense, technology, production, automation, AI/compute, drones, energy abundance and financial/industrial capacity.
entries.notes: Strategic autonomy is not synonymous with isolation from the United States.

entries.summary: Proposes radically re-evaluating US defense and other spending, reducing redundancy, reconsidering CIA/Pentagon/FBI structures peacefully, rebuilding selected domestic production, and redirecting capacity toward health, wealth, education, housing, energy and human outcomes.
entries.notes: Some numerical budget examples were hypothetical/ambiguous and are intentionally not normalized here.

entries.summary: Audit each public entity, programme, NGO, company or branch for measurable value; simplify, merge, repurpose, pause or remove structures sequentially rather than demolishing them ideologically and assuming replacements will work.
entries.notes: VAT and billionaire taxation were described as options on the table, not fixed universal doctrine.

entries.summary: Supports more northern European gas, less dependence on US LNG, expansion of wind/green energy and nuclear, stronger grids/electricity and energy surplus.
entries.notes: Pragmatic portfolio approach centered on resilience and productive capacity.

entries.summary: Uses NORTH/WEST/EAST/SOUTH as a relational map for political-economic systems and currencies rather than a simple nation list; Russia sits in East ‘for now’ while North remains a European/northern field.
entries.notes: Model mixes descriptive geopolitics with symbolic architecture and must be labeled accordingly.

entries.topic: Lobbying / cults / controlled opposition / Palantir / AIPAC / Israel365 / Figtree / Turning Point / Hollywood
entries.summary: Requests broad relational research into political funding, lobbying, religious-political networks, data/surveillance contractors, cultic dynamics, controlled-opposition hypotheses, media/Hollywood and victim networks.
entries.notes: Investigation interest is not evidence that the named actors are centrally coordinated. Each relationship requires sourcing, directionality, dates and confidence.

synthesis.core: Substantial freedom plus responsibility; markets and private property alongside public healthcare, education, infrastructure and a social floor; a state no larger than justified but capable enough to build strategic capacity; fiscal discipline; sovereign nations that cooperate deeply; European strategic autonomy; power constrained by legitimacy, reciprocity, transparency and outcomes rather than ideology.

unresolved: universal basic income as current doctrine
whether wealth tax is universal doctrine
